A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MotionAura study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VAE reconstruction, text-to-video generation and sketch-guided inpainting experiments, alongside ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds VAE controls, joint image/video training results, MCL-JCV compression results and UCF-101 generation results.

M1.justification: v1 specifies Euclidean nearest-neighbor vector quantization. v2 names lookup-free quantization as the default in Appendix B.2.1 but retains the nearest-neighbor description in Section 3.1. This leaves unclear whether the quantizer changed or the new documentation is inconsistent. The corresponding backbone, spectral-transformer, loss and LoRA descriptions otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds joint video/image training using JDB's Midjourney images, fixed-rate video-compression evaluation on MCL-JCV, and zero-shot generation evaluation on UCF-101. These substantially extend training and evaluation coverage beyond the retained reconstruction, MSR-VTT generation and DAVIS/YouTube-VOS inpainting experiments.

E2.justification: The new MCL-JCV comparison introduces HEVC, VCC (as labeled in Table 9), MAGVIT and MAGVIT-v2 as evaluated comparators. Existing reconstruction and generation comparator sets remain intact. Extending SimDA, AnimateDiff and CogVideoX-5B to UCF-101 does not itself introduce additional comparator identities.

E3.justification: New protocols include compression testing on 30 videos at 640×360 and 0.0384 bpp, joint training with N=1 for images and N≥16 for videos, and model-specific scheduler, guidance and step settings for UCF-101. Table 10 also reports cosine learning-rate decay for MotionAura, conflicting with v1's linear schedule and the retained linear description in v2 Appendix D.3. Rerunning the original experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct masked-frame-loss removal and joint-training comparisons in Table 1, quantization/codebook/embedding comparisons in Table 7, separate and combined masking removals in Table 8, and discrete-versus-continuous latent comparisons with a continuous-space loss ablation in Table 11. These substantially expand tests of the design choices beyond v1's retained FFT, sketch, text-length, LoRA-rank and positional-embedding analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use point estimates and retain the same 100-participant ranking description. Neither reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Original numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are retained. Added results include joint-training and ablation rows, MCL-JCV PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 29.09/0.922/0.089, and UCF-101 FVD of 219; these are new experiments, not improvements to the unchanged original scores. Section 5.1 also newly says loss removal decreases LPIPS, although Table 1 shows an increase, including 0.092 to 0.112 on COCO-Val.

T1.justification: The principal equations, diffusion objective and LoRA formula remain unchanged. Appendix E restates the masked-frame negative-log-probability loss and supplies conceptual motivation, without adding a mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims concerning 3D-MBQ-VAE, spectral discrete diffusion, recaptioning and novel sketch-guided video inpainting. The added experiments support these existing contributions rather than redefine their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of LFQ's vocabulary/efficiency advantages and the interaction between discrete representations and token-based decoders. It also introduces a substantive compression qualification: conventional codecs achieve higher PSNR/SSIM while the proposed model achieves better LPIPS. Appendix C.3 newly acknowledges possible artifacts from watermark-removal preprocessing.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial documentation of comparator hyperparameters, quantizer/codebook settings, masking schedules, temporal downsampling locations, joint-training inputs, and watermark-removal/StableVSR preprocessing. These disclosures do not alone establish changes to existing experiments. The abstract replaces a future release promise with a release statement and project link; hosted resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references connecting Fourier layers to GAFNet/GRIZAL, discrete modeling to D2Styler and VQ-Diffusion, and new experiments to joint-training, compression and preprocessing literature. It removes the Karras 2019 and 2020 references. The broad positioning and novelty claims remain stable; duplicate entries for already cited works do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: The main narrative, section sequence and conclusion are largely retained. Changes include author/header information, an acknowledgment, localized wording edits, expanded appendix explanations, regrouped architecture subsections and relocation of the LoRA discussion into Appendix F. The additions do not amount to a comprehensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the table presentation with dedicated displays for quantization, masking, compression, hyperparameters, latent-space comparisons and UCF-101 results, and enlarges Table 1. Existing figures and qualitative galleries are retained but several are repositioned, including separating the two sketch-result panels across pages. Table 3's caption also explicitly identifies MSR-VTT as the evaluation dataset.

improvement.justification: The new loss, masking and latent-space controls provide direct evidence missing from v1's explanations of its design choices. Additional benchmarks and implementation disclosures improve assessability, and the compression comparison exposes a useful performance tradeoff. These gains are tempered by unreconciled quantizer and training-schedule descriptions and the reversed LPIPS statement in Section 5.1, yielding a limited net improvement.
